NOMINAL_IS_OUTSIDE_ITS_OWN_FAMILY.conclusion: C_stat is paired with a central value that is not inside it over a quarter of the measured events. This is a Gate-5 / P5A-promotion question, not a reporting-tier question.

PRECEDENT_minerva_own_data_release.unreported_bins_are: all at LOW p_parallel (1.5-6 GeV) and HIGH pT — the theta_mu<20deg staircase corner, i.e. removed by the SIGNAL DEFINITION, not by a per-bin reporting judgement
PRECEDENT_minerva_own_data_release.paper_states: 'There are 144 degrees of freedom for these studies, as there are 12x13 bins minus 12 bins excluded due to the 20 degree angle requirement' and 'The empty region in the top left of the plot is due to the requirement that the muon must be within a 20 degree angle of the beamline. The area around this region has lower efficiencies due to a larger portion of the event muons missing MINOS at these larger angles.' — so bins ADJACENT to the hole have LOWER EFFICIENCY and are REPORTED ANYWAY

our_63_are_all_published_bins.cross_check: 224 independently matches the paper-grid count stated in AGENTS.md and derived here from bin_mapping.txt

published_stat_uncertainty_on_the_SAME_b.CAVEAT_not_like_for_like: MINERvA's is data-statistics on a standard-selection sample; ours is a bootstrap over a 2e6-row training subsample plus per-replica target refinement on an extended-phase-space full-event estimator. The comparison bounds how statistically hard those BINS intrinsically are; it is not a matched comparison of the same quantity. A factor of ~40 is nonetheless far outside what that mismatch explains.

PRECEDENT_minerva_own_data_release.conclusion: MINERvA reports every bin inside its declared phase space, including bins it says have lower efficiency; the only absent bins are those the angular cut removes. Worst reported fractional stat uncertainty in the whole release is 0.131.
